newsitem.title: USA: E.Baton Rouge, La., Parish eyes major school plan.
newsitem.headline: E.Baton Rouge, La., Parish eyes major school plan.

text.p: A consultant has recommended that Louisiana's East Baton Rouge Parish finance up to $921 million of public school improvements through higher sales and property taxes, The Advocate said Tuesday.

The proposal from Sverdrup Facilities Inc recommends a one-cent sales tax increase, which would raise the sales tax in the parish to nine percent, except for food and medicine. That would raise about $52 million of new revenues annually, which would initially be used for pay-as-you go construction funding, and later for technology, operations and maintenance.

The plan calls for a phased-in propety tax hike that would begin in 1998 and add 29 mills of additional property tax by 2005. The property tax increase would support $400 to $450 million of general obligation bonds, the consultants said.

The two tax increases could go before voters as early as November, school Superintendent Gary Mathews said. He said the bonds would be issued as late as possible during construction, describing the plan as "pay as you go as long as you can."
